summary: This Wikipedia list catalogs artists described as general purveyors of the acid rock genre, a loosely defined style that evolved from mid-1960s garage punk and helped launch the psychedelic subculture. The page notes that the style is defined by heavy, distorted guitars, drug-referencing lyrics, and long improvised jams, and that its boundaries with 1960s punk, proto-metal, and blues-based hard rock are tenuous. The list names about 40 bands and musicians, with references and see-also links to related psychedelic genre lists.
one_line: A Wikipedia list of about 40 artists described as acid rock, a loosely defined 1960s style evolved from garage punk.
key_facts: Acid rock is a loosely defined type of rock music that evolved out of the mid-1960s garage punk movement and helped launch the psychedelic subculture.
The acid rock style is generally defined by heavy, distorted guitars, lyrics with drug references, and long improvised jams.
Acid rock's distinctions from other genres can be tenuous, as much of the style overlaps with 1960s punk, proto-metal, and early heavy, blues-based hard rock.
The list states that it is dynamic and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness, and invites readers to add missing items with reliable sources.
The Artists section of the list contains 40 entries, including The 13th Floor Elevators, Black Sabbath, Cream, Deep Purple, The Doors, Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane.
Alice Cooper is listed with the qualifier 'late 60s work' and is cited to a 2012 Indy Week article by Chris Parker.
Pop Mašina is listed with three references, including a 2024 Music Box article reporting the death of Robert Nemeček, described there as founder and leader of Pop Mašina.
The Wikipedia article on Mick Farren cites a 31 July 2013 New York Times obituary describing him as a British Rock 'n' Roll Renaissance Man who died at 69.
The list's See also section links to List of psychedelic rock artists, List of psychedelic folk artists, List of psychedelic pop artists and List of neo-psychedelia artists.
The Bibliography cites Amy L. Fletcher's 2012 entry 'Acid Rock' in The Guide to United States Popular Culture, pp. 7–8.
Mitchell K. Hall's 2014 book The Emergence of Rock and Roll is cited for a chapter titled 'Psychedelia'.
The page was last edited on 9 March 2024 and its text is available under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike License 4.0.
The page is categorized under Lists of rock musicians by subgenre and Drug culture, Hippie movement and Psychedelic musical groups.
